rendered: The question's premise does not hold. The document does not say bare Al outperformed the carbon/Al collector at high current. It says the opposite: bare Al electrodes were prone to failure at these currents. The bare Al electrode showed signs of shorting, which the authors attribute to uneven plating caused by its higher nucleation overpotential. The failure data are only in the supplementary Figure S3.[1][2]  The carbon nucleation layer, by contrast, gave a low hysteresis at high current: 45 mV[3] . Bare Al's hysteresis at that high current is not reported in the text, so no bare Al value can be subtracted from it and the question of how much lower it was cannot be answered from this document. The only hysteresis comparison at that current is previous work using Cu electrodes, which[4] (this is not bare Al data).
